lead: A prolonged (post-term) pregnancy reaches 42+0 wk (294 days) or more. The commonest reason a pregnancy only looks post-term is wrong dates. Risks rise after 41 wk, so every woman needs a plan before 42 wk.
f: Post-date: past the EDD but under 42 wk · Postmaturity describes the baby, not the weeks · 5–10% reach 42 wk (under 5% with early scan dating) · Recurs in about 30% · CRL at 11–14 wk ± 5 days is the best dating; scan and LMP differ by over 5 days: use the scan · Never re-date from a late scan

sc: Booked at 30 wk, '42 wk' by LMP, irregular cycles → Confirm gestational age first

f: Usually unknown · Previous post-term pregnancy, primigravida, obesity, male fetus · Low fetal cortisol: anencephaly, adrenal hypoplasia, placental sulphatase deficiency · Failing placenta: fetal distress, oligohydramnios, cord compression, meconium · Good placenta: macrosomia, shoulder dystocia

Often none · Postmaturity syndrome (about 20%): long thin baby, peeling skin, long nails, no vernix, meconium staining · Fetal: stillbirth (intrapartum death 4 times after 42 wk), distress, oligohydramnios, meconium aspiration, macrosomia · Neonatal: hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, polycythaemia · Maternal: more induction, instrumental birth, CS, tears, PPH

sc: Peeling skin and long nails at 42 wk → Postmaturity syndrome; the same at 37 wk → FGR

f: Confirm dates; deliver earlier with PE, diabetes, FGR or APH · Membrane sweep at 40–41 wk (not with praevia or after ROM) · Offer induction from 41+0 wk (NICE 2021); local units often at 41+3 · Fewer stillbirths, no rise in caesareans · Declines: CTG + deepest pool twice a week, kick count · Induce now with low liquor (deepest pool under 2 cm), reduced movements, poor growth, abnormal CTG

sc: 41+4 wk, declined induction, deepest pool 1.5 cm → Induce now

f: Continuous CTG · Early ARM to see the liquor · Meconium + abnormal CTG → CS · Ready for shoulder dystocia · Neonatal team; active third stage

tr: Suctioning the mouth on the perineum to prevent meconium aspiration is not done
